content.text: Create a file named .env.example documenting only the NAMES (never values) of environment variables this project will need: DATABRICKS_HOST, DATABRICKS_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, ENTIRE_INGEST_URL, ENTIRE_INGEST_TOKEN. Add a short comment above each explaining its purpose, and a header note that real secrets must never be committed and belong in Databricks secret scopes. Then stage only .env.example and commit with message: chore: add .env.example documenting required env var names. Do not push.

input.file_text:
# Environment variable names required by this project.
# IMPORTANT: Real secrets must NEVER be committed to this file or the repository.
# Store actual values in Databricks secret scopes (or another secure secret manager)
# and inject them at runtime via environment variables.

# Hostname of the Databricks workspace used by this project (e.g., https://<workspace>.azuredatabricks.net)
DATABRICKS_HOST=

# Personal/service access token used to authenticate API calls to Databricks
DATABRICKS_TOKEN=

# Token used to authenticate with the GitHub API (e.g., for repo access or CI operations)
GITHUB_TOKEN=

# URL of the "Entire" ingest endpoint that receives data pushed from this project
ENTIRE_INGEST_URL=

# Authentication token used to authorize requests to the Entire ingest endpoint
ENTIRE_INGEST_TOKEN=

input.command: git add .env.example; git commit -m "chore: add .env.example documenting required env var names`n`nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>"
